summary: Crow's nest patrol point for Graham Mountain in the Coeur d'Alene NF; never a tower; a 2024 hike found a fallen nest tree, rock structure and wire.

facts.status_note: Never had a tower; the crow's nest tree had fallen by 2024, leaving a small rock structure and wire

visit.trail_note: Hike-in per Idaho Fire Lookouts; the hike is somewhat long but mostly downhill, and the trail out vanished after a few miles

events.note: Idaho Fire Lookouts hike: crow's nest tree main trunk fallen; small rock structure and #9 wire found; no tower ever present

evidence.supports: Elevation 4,870 feet; Coeur d'Alene National Forest
Crow's nest patrol point for Graham Mountain, two miles away
evidence.quote: Nira Point was a crows nest patrol point for Graham Mountain (2 miles away).

evidence.supports: Patrol began around 1922 by guess, when Graham Mountain was established
evidence.quote: Graham Mnt was first established in 1922 so we are guessing Nira Point began its history as a patrol point around the same time.

evidence.supports: Some question remains about what was located on the site
evidence.quote: There is there some question about what was located here

evidence.supports: Almost certainly never a tower of any kind
evidence.quote: we can almost certainly say there was never a tower of any kind

evidence.supports: Group believes it found the crow's nest tree, main trunk fallen
evidence.quote: We do believe we found the crows nest tree

evidence.supports: Crow's nest tree main trunk has fallen (2024 visit)
evidence.quote: although we think the main trunk has fallen down

evidence.supports: Small rock structure and fallen trunk with spikes next to the tree
evidence.quote: Right next to it we found this small rock structure and a fallen tree trunk with 2 large spikes driven into it.

evidence.supports: Small rock structure and a lot of #9 wire leading to the site
evidence.quote: We were also able to find a small rock structure and a TON of #9 wire leading to the site.

evidence.supports: Hike is somewhat long but mostly downhill
evidence.quote: The hike is somewhat long but mostly downhill.

evidence.supports: Trail out was very steep and vanished after a few miles
evidence.quote: the trail was very steep and completely disappeared after a few miles

evidence.supports: Crow's nest patrol atop Nira Point, two miles NNE of Graham Mountain
evidence.quote: There was also a crow's nest patrol atop Nira Point 2 miles

evidence.supports: Gary Weber joined the hike to look for the old site in the North Fork of the Coeur d'Alene River drainage
evidence.quote: Weber joined them on a recent hike to look for an old site at Nira Point in the North Fork of the Coeur d’Alene River drainage.

evidence.supports: Party found a few things suggesting they were in the right spot, but nothing major
evidence.quote: They found a few things that indicated they were in the right spot, but nothing major.

evidence.supports: On the way down the trail vanished and they bushwhacked
evidence.quote: On the way down, the trail they were using vanished, leaving them to bushwhack their way downhill.

sources.title: Top of the world: Idaho Fire Lookouts project traces the legacy of forest fire spotters

notes_for_editor: Kind: the site had no structure and the crow's nest was in a tree, so the vocabulary entry 'tree' (lookout tree, no structure) fits better than the brief's unknown; not written into facts. Status set to ruins (remains only), a judgement call since no tower ever stood. The 1922 date is a guess by the source and is left out of events. The site says no staffing history is documented, so staffing is left out. Spokesman title checked on 2026-10-21 against the spokesman.com page; it matches the footnote. Elevation 4,870 ft is in the story; record elevation_m stays null. County null in the record; not added.
